meta.title: Operation of Sample Storage Cabinet in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To store crude drug samples, reference standards, herbarium voucher specimens, and extract samples in an organized, secure, and climate-appropriate manner to ensure traceability and sample integrity.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for systematic storage and retrieval of crude drug repository samples, authenticated specimens, and working reference materials.
procedure: Assign a unique accession number to every sample before placing it in the storage cabinet.
Label each sample container with: accession number, drug name (botanical name and family), plant part, collection location, collection date, collector name, and storage condition.
Select the appropriate container type: airtight glass jars for powders; cloth bags for whole crude drugs; amber glass vials for extracts and standards.
Place desiccant (silica gel sachets) inside containers or shelves where moisture-sensitive drugs are stored.
Organize samples alphabetically by botanical name or by drug category on dedicated, labelled shelves.
Maintain a master inventory register (physical + digital) recording all samples with their location code (shelf-row-position).
Perform a monthly inventory check — verify physical samples against the register; report and investigate discrepancies.
Inspect all stored samples monthly for signs of: insect infestation, mould growth, moisture damage, or label deterioration.
Replace damaged labels immediately using waterproof permanent markers.
Fumigate the cabinet quarterly using thymol crystals or approved fumigant to prevent insect infestation.
Withdraw samples using the FIFO principle; log all withdrawals in the inventory register with date, quantity, purpose, and user.
Return unused portions of withdrawn samples promptly in correctly labelled containers.
Discard degraded, contaminated, or expired samples as per institutional waste disposal protocols.
Restrict access to authorized personnel only — maintain an access log.
precautions: Never store unlabelled or inadequately labelled samples — this violates GLP and PCI inspection requirements.
Keep the storage cabinet locked when not in use — access must be controlled and logged.
Maintain temperature and humidity within recommended limits: crude drugs generally 15–25°C, relative humidity < 60%.
Inspect regularly for insects (particularly dermestid beetles and moths) which are the primary pest threat to crude drug repositories.
Do not mix authenticated reference samples with unverified samples on the same shelf.
Store volatile drug materials (camphor, menthol-containing drugs) separately in sealed containers to prevent contamination of adjacent materials.
Ensure the cabinet is away from direct sunlight, moisture, and heat sources.
